title: Molecular arrangement of symmetric and non-symmetric triblock copolymers of poly(ethylene oxide) and poly(isobutylene) at the air/water interface.
text_summary: 本研究通过测量表面压力与平均分子面积等温线（p- mmA）、Langmuir-Blodgett（LB）技术和红外反射吸收光谱（IRRAS），研究了聚乙二醇（PEO）和聚异丁烯（PIB）对称和非对称三嵌段共聚物在空气/水界面的分子排列。研究发现，具有较长PEO段的三嵌段共聚物（PEO32-b-PIB160-b-PEO32）形成稳定的单分子层，并在p=5.7 mN/m处出现伪平台，这与IRRAS中观察到的PEO溶解到亚相和随后的PEO刷脱水的煎饼到刷的过渡有关。在p=40 mN/m处观察到另一个平台，这归因于由于多层形成而导致的薄膜塌陷。对于具有较短PEO链的共聚物，无法观察到煎饼到刷的过渡。具有短PEO链的共聚物（PEO3-b-PIBn-b-PEO3）的等温线在p=20-25 mN/m处显示出另一个过渡，这被解释为从中间PIB块通过端基亲水段锚定在水面两端的折叠状态到PIB在一端锚定在水面上的展开状态的构象转变。假设这种转变涉及从水面上移除PEO3链，在非对称PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3的情况下，以及在对称的情况下，可能是每个PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3链中的一个PEO3。由于较短的PEO3链与水面的相互作用比相对较长的PEO12链弱，因此PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3的薄膜在转变后比PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3在更低的表面压力下塌陷。原子力显微镜（AFM）图像显示，在PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3和PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3的LB薄膜转移到硅表面后形成了高度几乎均匀的微域（6-7 nm）。这些域被认为是有序和折叠的PIB链的液晶域。

Molecular arrangement of symmetric and non-symmetric triblock
copolymers of poly(ethylene oxide) and poly(isobutylene) at the air/
water interface

The behavior of a series of amphiphilic triblock copolymers of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and poly(iso-
butylene) (PIB); including both symmetric (same degree of polymerization (DP) of the terminal PEO
blocks) PEOm-b-PIBn-b-PEOm and non-symmetric (different DP of the terminal PEO blocks) PEOm-b-PIBn-
b-PEOz, is investigated at the air/water interface by measuring surface pressure vs mean molecular area
isotherms (p vs mmA), Langmuir–Blodgett (LB) technique, and infrared reﬂection–absorption spectros-
copy (IRRAS). The block copolymer (PEO32-b-PIB160-b-PEO32) with longer PEO segments forms a stable
monolayer and the isotherm reveals a pseudo-plateau starting at p  5.7 mN/m, also observed in the
IRRAS, which is assigned to the pancake-to-brush transition related to the PEO dissolution into the sub-
phase and subsequent PEO brush dehydration. Another plateau is observed at p  40 mN/m, which is
attributed to the ﬁlm collapse due to multilayer formation. The pancake-to-brush transition could not
be observed for samples with smaller PEO chains. The isotherms for block copolymers, with short PEO
chains, both symmetric (PEO3-b-PIBn-b-PEO3) and non-symmetric (PEO12-b-PIBn-b-PEO3), reveal another
transition at p  20–25 mN/m. This is interpreted to be due to the conformational transition from a
folded state where the middle PIB block is anchored to the water surface at both ends by the terminal
hydrophilic segments to an unfolded state with PIB anchored to the water surface at one end. It is
assumed that this transition involves the removal of PEO3 chains from the water surface in case of
non-symmetric PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3 and in case of symmetric, probably one PEO3 of each PEO3-b-
PIB85-b-PEO3 chain. Because of the weaker interaction of the short PEO3 chains with the water surface
as compared with the relatively longer PEO12 chains, the ﬁlm of PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3 collapses at much
lower surface pressure after the transition as compared with the PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3. The AFM images
reveal the formation of microdomains of almost uniform height (6–7 nm) in LB ﬁlms of PEO3-b-PIB85-b-
PEO3 and PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3 after transferring onto silicon surfaces. These domains are assumed to be
the mesomorphic domains of ordered and folded PIB chains.

1. Introduction
Amphiphilic block copolymers belong to a class of polymeric
materials that have the ability to create self-assembled nanostruc-
tures in selective solvents, thin ﬁlms, and bulk, which has led to
many applications for amphiphilic block copolymers in areas rang-
ing from water puriﬁcation [1], surface modiﬁcation [2], drug-
delivery systems [3], as templates to achieve ordered nanostruc-
tures [4], to anti-fouling surfaces [5]. Additionally, amphiphilic
block copolymers have been extensively investigated both theoret-
ically and experimentally to understand their molecular arrange-
ment and the formation of self-assembled nanostructures at the
air/water interface [6–13].
Similar to low molar mass amphiphiles, amphiphilic block
copolymers, composed of hydrophobic and hydrophilic segments,
have the ability to form a monomolecular layer at the air/water
interface. The hydrophilic block anchors the block copolymer to
the water subphase, while the hydrophobic block grafts the
copolymer chains to the air. By measuring the surface pressure
as function of mean molecular area during compression of the
monolayer, the so-called Langmuir isotherm also termed as surface
pressure vs mean molecular area (p–mmA) isotherm is recorded.
The p–mmA isotherm reveals various regimes corresponding to

various transitions and conformations of the block copolymer
chains at the interface during compression. For example, Langmuir
isotherms of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) containing amphiphilic
block copolymers show a pancake region at lower surface pressure
where the PEO chains are adsorbed on the water surface with a
ﬂattened conformation, followed by a pseudo-plateau which is
attributed to the dissolution of PEO chains into the water sub-
phase. The PEO chains adopt a brush conformation at higher sur-
face pressure and grafting density [14–16].
Amphiphlic block copolymers with PEO as the hydrophilic block
and polystyrene (PS) [17–19], poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA)
[14], poly(propylene oxide) [20], poly(L-lactide) [21], perﬂuori-
nated methacrylate [22–25], and many more [10,26,27] as the
hydrophobic block have been extensively investigated at the air/
water interface. More recently, our group has started investiga-
tions on a new series of PEO and polyisobutylene (PIB) containing
block copolymers for monolayer and nanostructure formation at
the air/water interface and has observed some unusual behavior
[28,29]. The Langmuir isotherms for PIB-b-PEO diblock copolymers
showed a typical plateau, corresponding to the pancake-to-brush
transition of PEO; however, with decreasing length of the PEO
chains, the plateau disappeared completely from the p–mmA iso-
therm. At higher surface pressures (p  41 mN/m) all the iso-
therms exhibited an extended plateau, corresponding to the
multilayer formation due to the so-called roll-over collapse of
the monolayer [30], which is known for PIB based amphiphiles
[31]. After transferring the monolayer of PIB130-b-PEO19 to silicon
substrate
using
the
Langmuir–Blodgett
(LB)
technique,
AFM
images revealed the formation of columnar structures of speciﬁc
heights perpendicular to the silicon substrate, which were ascribed
to the organization of PIB chains into mesomorphic domains. The
occurrence of mesomorphic PIB is surprising and interesting since
PIB is an amorphous polymer which shows crystallization only in
oriented ﬁbers under external stress [32]. In another study on
PIB-b-PEO three arm star block copolymers having very short
PEO (3EO units per arm) segments, the monolayer apparently col-
lapsed at relatively lower surface pressure (p = 22 mN/m) as indi-
cated by a transition in the compression Langmuir isotherm. The
typical plateau for the multilayer formation could not be observed.
The Langmuir isotherm of PIB-b-PEO star block copolymers with
relatively long PEO segments (16EO units per arm), without the
plateau corresponding to pancake-to brush transition, revealed
the formation of stable monolayer with a collapse pressure of
39 mN/m, with surface pressure still slightly increasing with fur-
ther compression. In the current study, we are aiming to extend
our understanding by investigating a series of triblock copolymers
of PEO and PIB (PEO-b-PIB-b-PEO) for their monolayer formation
and various phase transitions at the air-/water interface by mea-
suring the p–mmA isotherms, infra-red reﬂection–absorption spec-
troscopy (IRRAS), and atomic force microscopy (AFM) on LB ﬁlms.
The triblock copolymers under investigation differ in PIB–PEO ratio
and have different chain architectures, including; symmetric
PEO32-b-PIB160-b-PEO32,
PEO12-b-PIB55-b-PEO12,
PEO3-b-PIB57-b-
PEO3,
and
PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3
and
non-symmetric
PEO3-b-
PIB70-b-PEO12, and PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO12. For comparison pur-
poses, PIB homopolymers have also been investigated for their
monolayer formation at the air/water interface.
2. Experimental
2.1. Materials
The
investigated
PEO-b-PIB-b-PEO
triblock
copolymers
(Scheme 1 and Table 1) were synthesized and characterized as
described elsewhere [33,34].
2.2. Surface pressure measurements
Langmuir isotherm measurements were performed with a KSV
2000 Langmuir trough system (KSV, Helsinki) with a maximal sur-
face area of 76,050 mm2 equipped with symmetrically movable
barriers, a platinum Wilhelmy plate for surface pressure measure-
ments, and a circulating water bath system for temperature con-
trol. The subphase was puriﬁed deionized water (TKA GenPure
Labor&Reinstwassertechnick Christian Wiesenack, Jena) with a
conductivity <0.056 lS cm1. The surface purity of water in the
trough was checked before each measurement by surface pressure
measurements to a maximum compression (p < 0.15 mN m1).
Predetermined volumes (50 ll and 100 ll) of the block copolymer
solution, prepared in HPLC grade chloroform (1.0–2.0 mg/mL) were
spread evenly on the subphase with fully opened barriers using a
digital microsyringe.
The Langmuir isotherm measurements started after a waiting
period of 20 min to ensure the complete evaporation of chloroform
and uniform diffusion of the block copolymer chains on the water
surface. The compression rate was kept at 15 cm2/min. The com-
plete isotherm for each sample was obtained by multiple measure-
ments with increasing amount of spread volume, ranging from 100
up to 900 ll for the homopolymer and 20 to 200 ll for the triblock
copolymers, leading to different initial surface pressures. Thus, dif-
ferent regions of the isotherm were ﬁrst recorded and later com-
bined into one plot to produce a complete isotherm.
2.3. Infrared reﬂection absorption spectroscopy
Infrared reﬂection absorption spectroscopy (IRRAS) was per-
formed on a BRUKER Vector 70 FT-IR spectrometer equipped with
a nitrogen cooled MCT detector and an A511 reﬂection unit (Bruker
Optics, Germany), placed over the Langmuir trough setup (Riegler
& Kierstein, Germany). A trough with two compartments in a her-
metically sealed box was used. The sample trough (30  6 cm2)
was equipped with a Wilhelmy balance and two barriers. A circular
reference trough (r = 3 cm) placed next to the sample trough can be
brought into the focus of the IR beam by means of a shuttle. The
ﬁlling levels of both troughs were kept equal and constant by
means of an automated, laser reﬂection controlled, pumping sys-
tem connected to reservoirs of puriﬁed, deionized water. The IR
beam can be focused to the water surface in different angels of
incidence with respect to the surface normal and was polarized
with a KRS-5 wire-grid polarizer. The reﬂectance absorbance spec-
tra (RA) were calculated from the single-beam reﬂectance spectra
recorded on the reference (R0) and sample trough (R) according
to RA = log(R/R0). The resolution and scanner speed in all experi-
ments were 4 cm1 and 80 kHz. 1000 scans or 500 scans were
accumulated for measurements in p- or s-polarization, respec-
tively. A zero ﬁlling factor of 2 was applied before Fourier transfor-
mation, resulting in a ﬁnal data point distance of 2 cm1.
Two types of IRRAS experiments were performed:
(i) Spectra were recorded at 45 different areas during a PEO32–
PIB160–PEO32 monolayer compression from 1150 Å2/mole-
cule (2.5 mN/m) to 280 Å2/molecule (18 mN/m). The com-
pression speed was 30 Å2/(molecule min). However, during
spectra accumulation the barriers were stopped. Spectra
were recorded in p- and s-polarization at an angle of inci-
dence of 40.
(ii) Angle dependent measurements were performed on PEO32-
b-PIB160-b-PEO32 monolayer at three different surface pres-
sures (4; 10; 20 mN/m). The spectra were recorded in p-
and s-polarization and at various angles of incidence, rang-
ing from 25 to 70 in increments of 3 excluding 52, 55
and 58 due to the low reﬂectivity in the range of the Brew-

The subphase level was adjusted before each data acquisi-

2.4. IRRA spectra simulation and ﬁtting
IRRA spectra were simulated using a 3 layer model (subphase/
ﬁlm/air) as described in Schwieger et al. [36]. To determine the
layer thickness simulated spectra were ﬁtted to experimental ones
in a global ﬁt, were spectra recorded in different angles of inci-
dence (AoI) and polarization (p or s) were ﬁtted in one non-linear
least square minimization using the Levenberg–Marquardt algo-
rithm. Spectra were ﬁtted in the range of 3000–3600 cm1, which
corresponds to the OH stretching vibrational band m(OH). The opti-
cal constants of the subphase water were taken from Berti et al.
[37]. The polarizer quality C was set to 0.008 (0.8%) in all simula-
tion and ﬁts. The refractive index of the layer n, and the layer thick-
ness d were free ﬁtting parameter while ﬁtting angle and
polarization dependent spectra recorded at a PEO32-b-PIB160-b-
PEO32 surface pressure of 4 mN/m. For all other ﬁts n was set con-
stant to the determined value of 1.457 and d was the only ﬁtting
parameter. Spectra recorded at a AoI close to the Brewster angle
(46–58) were not included into the ﬁt due to their low signal-
to-noise ratio.
2.5. DFT calculation
DFT calculations were carried out with Gaussian 09 (Gaussian
Inc. Wallingford, CT). B3Lyp functional and 3-21g* basis set were
used to minimization and calculation of vibrational energies and
strengths. DFT calculation were performed on simple model mole-
cules as neopentan, 4,4-dimethyl heptan and PIB7.
2.6. Langmuir–Blodgett deposition
For Langmuir–Blodgett ﬁlm deposition silicon wafers were cut
into pieces of about 10  10 mm. The substrates were cleaned by
a modiﬁed RCA method [35]. At ﬁrst the wafers were treated with
H2O/H2O2/NH4OH (5:1:1) solution at 80 C for 5 min and after
cooling rinsed with deionized water and put in a H2O/H2O2/HCl
(5:1:1) solution at 80 C for 5 min. After that they were cooled
and rinsed with deionized water again. If not used immediately,
the cleaned silicon wafers were stored in deionized water. For LB
deposition, the cleaned silicon wafers were submerged into the
subphase before compression. The monolayer was allowed to sta-
bilize for 30 min after the desired surface pressure was reached.
Subsequently, the transfer onto the substrate was achieved at a
constant pressure by a vertical motion of the substrate through
the monolayer at a rate of 0.1 mm/min. The Langmuir–Blodgett
ﬁlms were dried in a desiccator at room temperature and stored
in a freezer if AFM measurement could not be performed
immediately.
2.7. Atomic force microscopy
The morphology of the LB ﬁlms was investigated using an
atomic force microscope (Nano Wizard, JPK Instruments, Berlin)
equipped with NT-MDT silicon cantilever with a resonance fre-
quency of 240–440 kHz and a force constant of 22–100 N/m.
3. Results and discussion
Prior to the investigation of block copolymers, the Langmuir
ﬁlm formation ability of poly(isobutylene) (PIB) homopolymers
of various molar masses (Mn = 1500, 7450, 21,500 g/mol) was
investigated.
However,
repeated
measurements
showed
no
increase in surface pressure with compression of PIB ﬁlm. It has
been known that nonpolar hydrocarbon (having only C and H
atoms) based polymers are poorly surface active and thus do not
form stable monolayers because they lack a group which allows
the polymer to interact with the water subphase [38]. Thus, it is
unlikely that the PIB homopolymer can form stable Langmuir ﬁlms.
Bernardini et al. [39] argue that PIB spreads in monolayer which
continuously thickens even at very low surface pressure. The only
way to achieve a stable monolayer of PIB is to attach hydrophilic
groups to the polymer chain which could anchor the hydrophobic
PIB chains at the air/water interface [29,40].
3.1. p–mmA Isotherms of PEO-b-PIB-b-PEO triblock copolymers
Fig. 1 depicts the p–mmA isotherms of (a) PEO32-b-PIB160-b-
PEO32 and (b) PEO12-b-PIB55-b-PEO12. In the compression isotherm
of PEO32-PIB160-PEO32, shown in Fig. 1a), various regions can be
identiﬁed, which correspond to polymer chain conformations or

conformational transitions during compression. At lower surface
pressure, a liquid expanded phase, where the block copolymer
chains stay at the air/water interface. At lower surface coverage,
the PEO chain because of its amphiphilic nature, adopts a ﬂattened
conformation on the water surface with maximum contacts with
the water surface, (pancake conformation) and the PIB segment,
because of its strong hydrophobic nature, would adopt a con-
densed globular state to avoid contacts with the subphase. A
pseudoplateau (between point 2 and 3) starting at p  5.7 mN/m,
which represents a transition to the pancake conformation of the
monolayer, can be seen in Fig. 1a), where the PEO chains submerge
into the water subphase during compression and anchor at the
water surface by the insoluble PIB segment of the block copolymer.
The extension of the plateau is strongly dependent on the length of
the PEO chain; it increases with increasing PEO chain length and
vice versa [25]. The plateau region is small and ill-deﬁned because
of the relatively short PEO chains as compared with the PIB seg-
ments in the block copolymer. Followed by the plateau is a sharp
increase in surface pressure with further compression, represent-
ing the brush conﬁrmation. The ﬁnal plateau at 40 mN/m, start-
ing at mmA 190 Å2, indicates the ﬁlm collapse, due to the
formation of multilayer structures on the water surface as reported
previously for PIB based amphiphiles [28]. The ﬁrst signiﬁcant
increase in surface pressure starts at 2900 Å2 (point 4 in the
Fig. 1a)).
The limiting pancake area was calculated of 2370 Å2 (point 5)
by extrapolation of a tangent to the pancake region as shown in
Fig. 1a). This area corresponds to 37 Å2 per EO unit for PEO32-b-
PIB160-b-PEO32 which is very close to the reported 40–48 Å2 area
per EO unit for PEO homopolymers [7,41]. This also suggests that
the area occupied by the PIB segments at the interface is negligible,
also reported for the PS block in PEO-b-PS block copolymers [7].
The cross-sectional area of a fully extended PIB chain is estimated
to be 55–60 Å2, [31] and for the current system, where the PIB
chain is supposed to form a loop in a fully stretched state on the
water surface, the cross-sectional could be calculated as 110–
120 Å2, thus, the collapse area 186 Å2 (point 1) depicted in
Fig. 1a) shows that the PIB chains are not fully extended. This
can be expected for higher molar mass long polymer chains, where
the coil structure is more stable.
Fig. 1b) depicts the p–mmA isotherms of PEO12-b-PIB55-b-PEO12,
where the pseudo-plateau could not be observed. This indicates
that the PEO chains in this block copolymer are too short to form
a pancake on the water surface and thus enter the subphase
directly after spreading without adopting a ﬂattened conformation.
This behavior is similar to PEO based amphiphilic block copoly-
mers with shorter PEO block [15]. In this isotherm, the ﬁrst
increase in surface pressure starts at 370 Å2 (point 2 in the
respective isotherm). The surface pressure increases almost line-
arly until the ﬁlm collapse as indicated by the plateau at 37 mN/
m (point 1). The mmA corresponding to the sharp increase in sur-
face pressure with compression is determined 322 Å2 by extrap-
olating the steep part of the isotherm to p = 0 (point 3). The area
occupied by a PIB55 chain, using Material Studio, was calculated
640 Å2 which is much larger than the experimentally determined
area per PIB55 chain at point 3 in Fig. 1b). This discrepancy in the
observed and expected molecular area could be due to the strong
hydrophobicity of the PIB chain which might form a loop to avoid
contact with the water surface. A similar discrepancy in molecular
area on the water surface has been reported for polystyrene mono-
layer on the water surface [42].
Fig. 2a) depicts the Langmuir isotherms of the triblock copoly-
mers having very short hydrophilic PEO terminal groups (3EO
units); PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3. Again due to short terminal PEO seg-
ments, the PEO related pseudo-plateau is missing from the iso-
therm.

with compression has been frequently reported for hydroxy fatty

[47–49]. At low surface pressure both the hydroxyl and the car-

compression, a point is reached when the hydroxyl group is

This transition involves a conformational change from a folded
conformation, where both the polar hydroxyl and carboxyl groups
are in the water subphase, to an erect state with the hydroxyl

The squeeze out of hydration water would increase the packing

in a more crowded polymer layer. Here, this dehydration process

method helps to understand details of the transition process. From
comparison of the ﬁlm compressibility and the m(OH) band inten-

consecutive processes and not occurring simultaneously.

4. Conclusions
The behavior of poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and poly(isobutyl-
ene) (PIB) containing amphiphilic triblock copolymers; PEO-b-
PIB-b-PEO, containing both symmetric (same degree of polymeri-
zation (DP) of the terminal PEO) and non-symmetric (having differ-
ent DP of the terminal PEO chains) block copolymers, is evaluated
at the air/water interface. The Langmuir isotherm of symmetric tri-
block copolymer with relatively longer terminal PEO segments
(PEO32-b-PIB160-b-PEO32) revealed a pseudo-plateau starting at
p  5.7 mN/m that is ascribed to the PEO related pancake-to-brush
transition during which the dissolution of PEO chains in water sub-
phase takes place, while another plateau at p  40 mN/m was
assumed to be due to multilayer formation as reported previously
for PIB-b-PEO diblock counterparts with longer PEO segments [28].
Thus, the molecular organizations of di- and triblock copolymers
with longer PEO segments are the same at the water surface.
A new transition was observed at p  20–25 mN/m in the iso-
therms of block copolymers with short PEO chains, both symmetric
(PEO3-b-PIBn-b-PEO3) and non-symmetric (PEO12-b-PIBn-b-PEO3).
This was attributed to conformational change of the monolayer
from a state where the middle PIB block is attached to the water
surface at both ends by the terminal PEO segments to an unfolded
state with PIB attached to the water surface at one end. The tran-
sition involves forcing out of PEO3 chains from the water surface
in case of non-symmetric (PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3) monolayer and
probably one PEO3 segment of each PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3 chain in
monolayer. We are not aware of such transition reported for mon-
olayers of block copolymers at the air/water interface. However,
there are a few reported examples of such behavior from the mon-
olayers of lower mass amphiphiles equipped with two unequal
polar groups located at a distance from each other in the amphi-
phile molecule [47–49]. Finally, microdomain formation was
observed in the AFM images of the Langmuir–Blodgett ﬁlms of
PEO3-b-PIB85-b-PEO3, PEO12-b-PIB85-b-PEO3, and PEO32-b-PIB160-
b-PEO32 transferred to silicon substrates. The microdomains of
almost uniform height (6–7 nm) in LB ﬁlms for the PIB85 block
are assumed to be the mesomorphic domains of ordered and
folded PIB chains. The PIB160 block has a domain height of approx-
imately 14 nm. Thus, it can be concluded that this triblock copoly-
mer shows a similar formation of mesomorphic domains as diblock
copolymers.
In general the length of the different blocks and the polymer
architecture inﬂuence the polymer behavior at the air/water inter-
face. With decreasing PIB block length the surface pressure at the
ﬁlm collapse decreases. This can be explained by the higher mobil-
ity of the polymer molecules on the water surface when the hydro-
phobic block becomes shorter. If a PEO3 block is present in a
symmetric (PEO3-b-PIBn-b-PEO3) as well as in a non-symmetric
architecture (PEO12-b-PIBn-b-PEO3) the anchoring of the polymer
on the water surface becomes weaker and further compression
leads to the forcing out of the PEO3 from the water subphase. This
is observed as a transition in the respective isotherms. However, a
higher surface pressure at the ﬁlm collapse is still reached for a
non-symmetric architecture compared to the symmetric one due
to the PEO12 block which remains in the subphase and increases
the resistance of the ﬁlm against further compression more
efﬁciently.

这是一张化学结构式图片（Figure 4），展示了两种聚合物的分子结构。上方为“PEO-b-PIB-b-PEO”的结构，其中n的取值为57、70或85，m的取值为3或12；下方为另一种聚合物的结构，n的取值为55或160，m的取值为12或32。结构中包含苯环、醚键、偶氮基（-N=N-）等基团，以及聚氧化乙烯（PEO）和聚异丁烯（PIB）的重复单元，整体呈现两种嵌段聚合物的分子式设计。

图5包含两张折线图，分别标记为(a)和(b)。(a)图展示的是聚合物PEO₃₂ - PIB₁₆₀ - PEO₃₂的表面压力（单位：mN/m）随平均分子面积（单位：Å²）的变化关系，横坐标为平均分子面积（范围约100 - 1000 Å²），纵坐标为表面压力（范围0 - 40 mN/m），曲线呈现表面压力随平均分子面积增大而下降的趋势，图中标注了5个点（1 - 5），分别对应不同的平均分子面积和表面压力数值（如点1：186 Å²、40 mN/m；点2：543 Å²、7.2 mN/m等）。(b)图展示的是聚合物PEO₁₂ - PIB₅₅ - PEO₁₂的表面压力随平均分子面积的变化关系，横纵坐标与(a)图一致，曲线同样呈现表面压力随平均分子面积增大而下降的趋势，图中标注了3个点（1 - 3），对应不同的平均分子面积和表面压力数值（如点1：95 Å²、37 mN/m；点2：409 Å²、0.1 mN/m等）。

图6包含两张折线图，分别标记为(a)和(b)。图(a)展示分子结构为PEO₃-PIB₈₅-PEO₃时，表面压力（mN/m）随平均分子面积（Å²）的变化关系；图(b)展示分子结构为PEO₃-PIB₈₅-PEO₁₂时，表面压力（mN/m）随平均分子面积（Å²）的变化关系。两张图横坐标均为“mean molecular area (Å²)”，纵坐标均为“surface pressure (mN/m)”。图(a)曲线标记1 - 4点，对应不同平均分子面积与表面压力（如1: 74 Å² 23 mN/m，2: 132 Å² 20 mN/m，3: 225 Å² 0.3 mN/m，4: 208 Å²）；图(b)曲线标记1 - 7点，对应不同平均分子面积与表面压力（如1: 60 Å² 38 mN/m，2: 100 Å² 28 mN/m，3: 140 Å² 22 mN/m，4: 261 Å² 2.7 mN/m，5: 435 Å² 0.1 mN/m，6: 232 Å² 3 mN/m，7: 413 Å²）。整体趋势为：随平均分子面积增大，表面压力呈下降趋势，不同分子结构下曲线下降幅度与关键点数值存在差异。

图7是分子排列示意图，展示了不同嵌段共聚物在低表面压力和高表面压力（坍塌前）下的分子构象变化。上半部分为“低表面压力下的分子排列”，呈现了多种嵌段共聚物（如PEO₃-b-PIB₈₅-b-PEO₃、PEO₃-b-PIB₈₅-b-PEO₁₂、PEO₁₂-b-PIB₅₅-b-PEO₁₂、PEO₃₂-b-PIB₁₆₀-b-PEO₃₂）的分子构象；下半部分为“坍塌前高表面压力下的分子排列”，分为“转变前”“转变时”“进一步压缩”三个阶段，展示了不同共聚物（如PEO₃-b-PIB₈₅-b-PEO₃和PEO₃-b-PIB₈₅-b-PEO₁₂在转变前，PEO₃₂-b-PIB₁₆₀-b-PEO₃₂和PEO₁₂-b-PIB₅₅-b-PEO₁₂在转变前；转变时和进一步压缩时的分子构象演变），呈现分子链在压力变化过程中的伸展、压缩及构象调整等变化。

图8是一张折线图，展示的是不同入射角（angle of incidence，单位为°）下羟基（ν(OH)）的最大强度（max. intensity of ν(OH)）的变化情况。横轴为入射角，范围是25 - 70°；纵轴为羟基的最大强度。图中包含多条不同颜色的折线（如蓝色、红色、黑色等），各折线代表不同条件下的数据。整体趋势为：随着入射角的增加，各折线的羟基最大强度先逐渐上升，在约45 - 50°左右达到峰值，之后随入射角继续增大而下降，最终趋于平缓。

Figure 9是一张光谱图（红外光谱图），包含主图a和多个放大子图（b、c、d、e、f、g、h）。主图a的横坐标为波数（wavenumber，单位cm⁻¹），范围4000 - 1000 cm⁻¹；纵坐标为-log R/R₀×10⁻³，展示不同样品或条件下的光谱信号。主图a中在约3500 cm⁻¹附近有显著强峰，随波数降低信号逐渐减弱。子图b是2800 - 3000 cm⁻¹区域的放大，子图d - g是1200 - 1500 cm⁻¹左右区域的放大，子图c和h是中间区域的放大，这些子图展示了不同波数范围内光谱峰的细节，不同颜色曲线代表不同样品或条件，体现光谱峰的强度、位置等差异。

图10是一张包含散点图和折线图的科学图表。横轴为1/mmA（单位nm⁻²），左纵轴表示ν(OH)的积分强度（integral intensity of ν(OH)），右纵轴表示可压缩性（compressibility，单位mN⁻¹）。图中包含三条不同颜色的散点序列（绿色、蓝色、紫色），各散点序列随横轴数值增大，左纵轴的积分强度和右纵轴的可压缩性均呈上升趋势，且不同颜色散点对应不同斜率的趋势线；此外还有一条黑色曲线，其趋势为先下降后上升再下降。

- 子图(c)：左侧AFM图像展示材料PEO₃₂-PIB₁₆₀-PEO₃₂的表面形貌，呈现大量小而密的凸起；右侧折线图包含三条高度剖面曲线，标注凸起高度约为14 nm。
